key_insight: MaGE uses whole-blood DNA methylation to estimate senescence-marker gene expression, creating a scalable proxy for cellular senescence in humans.
clinical_relevance: This could help stratify patients and support population-scale studies or senolytic trial design by linking senescence signals to disease risk and severity.
method: Built methylation-based predictors for p14ARF, p16INK4A, p21CIP1, and a composite score.
Applied the proxies to large human cohorts to test links with incident disease and mortality.
Validated disease-specific signals, including associations with pulmonary fibrosis, alcoholic liver disease, and Crohn’s disease severity/treatment response.
evidence_signal: In Generation Scotland (n=18,859), MaGE showed 45 Bonferroni-significant associations across 18 incident diseases and all-cause mortality.
watch_item: Because MaGE is derived from whole blood, tissue specificity and downstream clinical interpretation may be limited for diseases driven by other organs.
paper_title: Methylation-associated Gene Expression (MaGE): a non-invasive, in vivo measure of cellular senescence.
